source: a16z Podcast — AI demand outrunning compute supply; frontier-lab revenue is self-determined, reinvestment math, not necessarily winner-take-all
summary: Compute supply will be structurally undersupplied through at least 2028, driven by political/regulatory delays and fundamental material constraints
summary_extended: Baker argues that AI compute will be structurally undersupplied through at least 2028, making him far more concerned about massive undersupply than the consensus overbuild narrative. He supports this view by noting that all forecast datacenter builds through 2028 are already fully committed with no available capacity, and those builds face additional delays from political and regulatory dynamics. Binding material constraints — specifically citing copper, wafers, and other raw materials — compound the supply problem alongside rising real rates. The investment implication is that token prices could rise dramatically rather than deflate, with Andreessen Horowitz citing a potential 10x increase in token costs; this environment favors infrastructure providers and commodity suppliers tied to datacenter buildout over the consensus deflationary AI narrative. Baker frames this as a contrarian structural view where the primary risk is not overbuilding but chronic underinvestment relative to demand.
detail: Baker states there is no available capacity with all forecast builds through 2028, and those builds are now likely delayed due to political dynamics. He is more worried about massive undersupply than overbuild. Copper, Watson wafers, and other raw materials are becoming binding constraints. Rising real rates and regulation compound the supply problem. This could lead to token price increases (Andreessen Horowitz cited a potential 10x token cost increase) rather than the consensus deflation narrative.
